question: Can Russia keep its old bombers flying, yes or no?

lines.text: A Russian Tu-95 strategic bomber has crashed in the Amur region, in Russia's far east.
lines.note: Russian MoD via Moscow Times, 29 Sep 2026

lines.text: Russia's defence ministry says it was on a training flight, with no munitions on board.
It came down near Krasnoyarovo, thirty kilometres north of Ukrainka air base.
Seven crew were on board. The ministry says six died and one is in hospital.
lines.note: Russian MoD via Jerusalem Post, UNN

lines.text: No official cause yet. Telegram channels claim three of its four engines failed.
lines.note: Unverified claim, cited by UNITED24 and NV

lines.text: The Tu-95 is one of the planes Russia uses to fire Kh-101 cruise missiles at Ukraine.
The Moscow Times calls Ukrainka one of Russia's largest long-range air force bases.
It sits more than six thousand kilometres from Kyiv.
lines.note: Great-circle distance, Ukrainka to Kyiv, about 6,300 km

lines.text: In June 2025, Ukraine's Operation Spiderweb targeted it too, but the drone truck caught fire.
Russia stopped building Tu-95s decades ago, so it cannot replace this one with a new one.
It is Russia's third military plane crash reported this year, the Jerusalem Post says.
An air force commission is now at the site. Can Russia keep its old bombers flying, yes or no?
lines.note: UNN: Aerospace Forces commission sent to the site
